newsitem.title: CANADA: Still no deal in Inco /Sudbury union talks.
newsitem.headline: Still no deal in Inco /Sudbury union talks.

text.p: Contract talks between Inco Ltd's Ontario division and the union representing about 4,700 workers continued on Friday but the union said it was not optimistic a deal could be reached ahead of the midnight May 31 (0400 GMT Sunday) strike deadline.

"Let me tell you, unless there is something substantial on the table today, (operations are) down, and I can't put it any plainer than that," Gary Patterson, vice-president of Steelworkers' local 6500, said in a telephone interview from Sudbury.
The union on Thursday rejected Inco's latest offer.
Patterson said union negotiators met with union stewards late on Thursday and the group unanimously recommended rejection of Inco's Thursday offer.
"Now if they were meeting last night there may be more on the table today, but certainly what they came with last night didn't even come close to meeting our demands," he said.

Union membership meetings were scheduled for 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, 1700 EDT/2100 GMT and 2000 EDT/2400 GMT on Friday to inform workers of the latest rejection recommendation, but a vote would not take place until Monday.
Both sides said negotiations were continuing today.

Patterson said if a deal was not been reached by late on Saturday, the last shift of workers, which begins at 2300 EDT/0300 GMT Sunday, would not be sent in. If a tentative deal was reached before the midnight strike deadline, operations would continue until Monday's vote.
"If they haven't put anything else on the table, then it's rejected Saturday night at midnight (0400 GMT Sunday)," Patterson said.
Inco spokesman Jerry Rogers said the company was still hopeful a tentative agreement could be reached.
"We've been meeting around the clock for about 48 hours now, and we're hopeful of a new agreement. We're still talking," Rogers said.
He declined to comment on the union's latest contract offer or on the issues that remained on the table.
"I'm not going to get into any details. I'm just saying that we're hopeful at this point," Rogers said.
On Monday, the Steelworkers requested the assistance of a provincial mediator after talks reached an impasse last weekend.
Union members have voted 98 percent in favor of giving union leaders the mandate to strike if a tentative agreement cannot be reached by May 31.
The contract affects 4,700 workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne, Ontario.
